Thanks — quick note from commercial side. Two routing options for Acme:

Option A — Invoice amendment (Nov):
- We recalc Nov pro rata for 10–30 Nov; reissue Nov invoice with amended lines.
- Pros: single invoice; clear accounting for Nov.
- Cons: requires signed acceptance for amended invoice (customer ops overhead).

Option B — Credit on Dec invoice:
- Leave Nov invoice as-is; apply a negative line item on Dec 1 that reflects the prorated delta.
- Pros: simpler for procurement (no reissue).
- Cons: customer sees adjustment in next period; may complicate month-end numbers.

Commercially we can offer to absorb up to 5% of the prorated charge as a one-off promotional credit for the campaign if that helps the renewal conversation. If Acme prefers the credit route we can set that up quickly.

Happy to sync on a 15-min call.

Ben Carter
Senior Sales Manager, Redwood Inference

Hi all —

Regarding VAT/reverse-charge: to suppress VAT on the invoice we need the following from Acme (EU customer):
1) Company VAT registration number (format depends on member state).
2) Confirmation that the purchase is for business use (standard statement is fine).
3) A copy of the VAT registration certificate or screenshot from VIES if available.

If we have that before we finalize the invoice, we will apply reverse-charge wording on the invoice and show 0% VAT with a note. If we do the Dec credit route, the credit line will carry the same VAT treatment as the original supply — so please provide VAT evidence ASAP.

On proration math: for capacity we prorate by seat-days (seat x number of days active in the billing period) divided by days in month. Example attached with worked numbers for Nov (I used 30 days).

Attachment: Proposed_Pruning_PRORATE.xlsx (Excel)

Laura Bennett
